intended_object: The degree (0,1) cup product H⁰(G,M) × H¹(G,N) → H¹(G,P) in continuous group cohomology, taken with respect to a G-equivariant, jointly continuous biadditive pairing μ : M × N → P. On inhomogeneous cochains it is (m ⌣ b)(g) = μ(m, b(g)). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation, which cite Neukirch–Schmidt–Wingberg I §4 and Brown V §3.
explanation:
Here H0 is the fixed-point subgroup M^G, and H1 is Z¹/B¹, with Z¹ the continuous 1-cocycles and B¹ the coboundaries g ↦ g•n − n.

For a fixed invariant m, `pairingLeft` gives the map μ(m, ·) : N → P. It is G-equivariant precisely because m is invariant: μ(m, g•x) = μ(g•m, g•x) = g•μ(m, x). It is continuous because μ is jointly continuous.

The definition sends m to the coefficient map that `explicitCoeff1` induces on H¹ from μ(m, ·). That map is postcomposition b ↦ (g ↦ μ(m, b(g))), and the lemma `explicitCup01_mk` confirms this formula. This is the standard formula (a ⌣ b)(g₁,…,g_{p+q}) = μ(a(g₁,…,g_p), (g₁⋯g_p)•b(…)) at p = 0, where the empty product acts trivially.

Additivity in m is proved inside the definition, and additivity in the class of b holds because the coefficient map is a homomorphism. So the result is a biadditive map H⁰ → H¹ → H¹, as a cup product should be.

The generality is at least the natural one. G is only a topological monoid. The coefficients need only be topological abelian groups with continuous actions, which the continuous-cochain model needs anyway. The pairing is the standard data of an equivariant, continuous biadditive map. Mathlib has no cup product for group cohomology, continuous or not, so there is no counterpart to compare with.
